title: markdown-notion-alternative: add 'docs plus database' framing from brand session
description:
Notion's trick was docs *plus*: small databases and catalogues where each page is a record, all in one fluid space for a wiki, a personal knowledge base and team docs. Markdown can do both halves. A markdown file is a document, and with frontmatter it's also a database record ([[markdown-database]]). Obsidian bases and Flowershow catalogues build on that, and their UX is catching up. So markdown is a real competitor to Notion for most of what people use it for ([[markdown-notion-alternative]]). The honest limits (real-time co-editing, how polished the databases feel) belong on that page, checked rather than assumed.

Moved out of docs/brand.md (page content, not narrative). Rufus's own words in docs/raw/2026-10-02-brand-dictation.md section 6 (last two paragraphs); he has written posts on this. Check Notion's current markdown import/export before publishing. Voice rules apply.

title: Blog post: how markdown's tools caught up (the story of the way)
description: Rufus, 2026-10-02 (brand session): markdown was clearly less capable than Google Docs/Notion, a geeky format spread via text boxes on the web, and gradually took over; AI (voice/chat interfaces that speak markdown) accelerated it. Clayton Christensen Innovator's Dilemma framing. Second strand: composability. You don't get everything Notion does, but most of it, and better, by chaining open tools: Obsidian to edit, Git/GitHub for versions, Flowershow to publish. Draft from Rufus's dictation; voice rules apply. Candidate source for the Why area.
notes: 2026-10-02 Rufus: NOT 'the worse format won' (compares absolutes, poor phrasing). Story is the tooling: UX started as a web text box; open-source ecosystem (Obsidian WYSIWYG etc.) improved year on year; not quite Notion yet but closing; together they compose. That ecosystem is 'the way'.

title: Create a memorable Markdown tai chi animation for the homepage hero
description:
Migrated from GitHub issue https://github.com/flowershow/wayofmarkdown/issues/71 (comments stay there).

## Idea

Create a memorable animated visual for the homepage hero that gives The Way of Markdown a stronger, more distinctive identity.

The starting concept: a human figure doing tai chi or qigong movements, with the figure itself drawn from Markdown characters and markup — for example `#`, `*`, `_`, `>`, brackets, backticks and links. The movement should feel calm and recognisable, and the Markdown construction should be legible enough that the visual belongs specifically to this project rather than being a generic animation.

Source note:

> ➕ 2026-08-01 [plan-03w] Cool animation with Markdown markup, e.g. show a figure doing tai chi or qigong moves with the figure made of those symbols for @wayofmarkdown.

## Why

The site needs stronger, more memorable branding. The hero is the clearest place to establish that identity, and the combination of “the way” / movement with visible Markdown syntax could become a useful signature for the project.

## First pass

- [ ] Explore 2–3 visual directions for a Markdown-character tai chi/qigong figure
- [ ] Decide what the animation should communicate in the first few seconds
- [ ] Prototype a lightweight, responsive hero animation
- [ ] Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` and provide a strong static fallback
- [ ] Check legibility and visual impact on desktop and mobile
- [ ] Keep page weight and rendering performance reasonable

## Related homepage work

This may sit inside a broader homepage improvement rather than remain a standalone asset:

- The landing page body is already substantially HTML, so consider moving the homepage to a purpose-built HTML + Tailwind structure rather than relying on Markdown-generated page structure.
- The homepage should not show the normal sidebar.
- The homepage should not show giscus comments.
- Review the whole hero composition and branding around the animation, not only the animation in isolation.

Those items may deserve a separate parent/follow-up issue once the desired homepage direction is clearer. This issue should begin with the memorable hero visual and use it to inform that broader direction.

## Done when

There is an approved hero direction and a working, accessible, responsive prototype that feels recognisably “Way of Markdown,” with the broader homepage changes either included here or split into clearly linked follow-up work.

Related to #67.
close_reason: Hero mark and tai chi animation shipped (hero-mark.html, assets/brand/)

title: Blog post: why markdown is hard to explain (loop, two audiences, paradox)
description: From the 2026-10-02 brand session. Three reasons the markdown story resists a one-liner: (1) it's a loop (people write it ↔ tools support it, to critical mass), not a line; (2) the cause is for builders, the payoff is for users; (3) a format matters even though nobody cares about formats (TCP/IP vs banking/shopping online). Ends on the offer: 'The tools are good now. You can switch, and you own your files.' (files over app, not privacy). Companion to wom-bc1. Source: docs/brand.md 'Why this is hard to say' + docs/raw/2026-10-02-brand-dictation.md sections 8-9. Voice rules apply.
